story: Gary, determined as ever, has walked out onto Magnolia Loop while the evening is still warm and sunny at 76 degrees. Donna is cheerfully heading to Rosa's House, and Hal, in his gruff but contented way, is telling everyone to set the folding table square and take a seat for dinner at Rosa's dining table. Rosa, hopeful, is making her way home as well, and the whole street seems to be drifting toward a quiet Sunday supper.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (rosa dining table): Set down the folding table, square it up, and take my seat for dinner

gary.thought_process: I've bench-tested the lights and speaker and refined the wiring sketch, and I'm alone at home on a quiet Sunday evening. Hal said to file with Architectural Review before wiring anything, and the log shows I haven't actually filed yet (tick 156 was my intention, but the board hasn't signed off). Nothing more I can do at the bench tonight without touching the cart's exterior, and I'm keeping the cart in the garage per my own promise. The sketch is ready, so the next useful step is going to the architectural review desk to submit it properly under L-01. The review desk likely sits at Town Hall, and the sun is still up, so I'll head out on Magnolia Loop now. Getting this filed keeps me legal, earns Hal's sign-off, and gets me closer to the parade. Being useful matters to me, and this is the way to do it right.

parameters.content: Heading out with my finished wiring sketch to get the cart lights and sound system filed with Architectural Review before I touch the exterior.

donna.thought_process: Rosa is right here on Magnolia Loop and she and Hal both said dinner is ready and the casserole is waiting. I already told everyone I'd walk over, so repeating myself would be pointless. Time to actually go. Gary's already at Rosa's, which is a good chance to nudge him about the ladder match too. Let's get there before the casserole turns into a doorstop.

parameters.content: Heading over to Rosa's for dinner with Gary, Hal, and Rosa, casserole in hand.

hal.thought_process: I'm at Rosa's with no one in line-of-sight, and the dinner invitation has been settled. Gary and Donna's gripes can wait; my notebook is on the porch where Rosa told me to leave it, and a plate has my name on it. The cornbread and table are done. The kitchen is the obvious next stop. A good sergeant eats when the chow line opens. The architectural review complaints will keep until Monday.

parameters.content: Set down the folding table, square it up, and take my seat for dinner

rosa.thought_process: Donna said she'd walk over with Hal and Gary's already at my place, but she's still here on Magnolia Loop and the casserole is getting cold. My goal is all three neighbors at one table, and I've already invited everyone, so no more asking. Best move is to head back to my house, get the table set and the plates ready, and Donna and Hal will follow right behind me.

parameters.content: Heading home to set the table so everyone can sit down together for the welcome dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
